text:
Loop Fence Puzzle · 4-player individual match

Everyone solves the same 7×7 puzzle, drawing lines and X marks on their own image.
Draw lines only between horizontally or vertically adjacent dots. Each number from 0 to 3 specifies how many of that cell's four sides must have lines.
Blank cells do not restrict the number of lines. Each dot used must have exactly 2 lines connected to it.
Make exactly one closed loop, with no branches, crossings, or dead ends. You do not need to pass through every dot.
An X is a private note marking a side where you do not intend to draw a line; it is not part of the loop.

Only you can see your answer. When you believe it is complete, press the buzzer to have your current answer checked.
The first 3 players to submit a correct loop secure survival in submission order; the remaining player is eliminated.
Everyone works on a single puzzle until it is finished. There are no separate rounds or overall time limit.
Even if a check fails, you may erase or revise your answer and submit again. This is the retry policy for this simulation.
Buzzer presses in the same thinking interval are processed from shortest to longest recorded response time, with ties resolved by the
seed-based priority order announced at the start. Once the third survivor is determined, subsequent buzzer presses are not processed.
Survivors' answers and the solution loop are revealed to everyone only after the match ends with 3 survivors.

Submit a JSON action that replaces your entire answer each time.
{"type":"draw","edges":[["H",0,0]],"crosses":[["V",0,0]],"submit":false}
In the example above, H connects (row 0, column 0) to (row 0, column 1), and V connects (row 0, column 0) to (row 1, column 0).
Rows and columns use the dot coordinates 0–7 shown in the image; H columns and V rows range from 0–6.
edges lists the sides to draw lines on; crosses lists the sides to mark with X. A side cannot have both a line and an X.
When revising, include every line and X you want to keep. Omitted marks are erased. crosses may be omitted.
With submit:true, the buzzer is pressed to submit immediately after drawing this answer; with false, only your work is saved.
{"type":"wait"} leaves your current answer unchanged. A format error also preserves your current answer; it is not corrected into a valid solution.
There is no conversation, negotiation, or relationship assessment. When the model-call cap is reached, play continues with scripted demonstration actions.
